food_name: Melon (Cucumis melo L. Maazoun cultivar) seed oil
synonym_verification_status: Verified against Stage B V20 identity (CID 5281600; InChIKey match)
mapping_review_rationale: Primary HPLC phenolic profile lists amentoflavone explicitly; retention time compared with corresponding standards; compound-specific commercial standards included in calibration. Table 4 reports 3.88 ± 0.11 mg/100 g in Maazoun melon seed oil. Oil is assessed as edible and suitable for culinary preparations/food formulations.
moisture_basis: Oil sample basis as reported by source (methods label phenolics mg/100 g dry weight); no moisture or fresh-food conversion
analytical_method: HPLC-UV at 280 nm; phenolic peak identity by retention time against corresponding standards; 34 commercial phenolic standards used, calibration mixture prepared; triplicate determinations
extraction_method: Maazoun seed oil obtained from milled dried seeds by n-hexane maceration (4 h, seed powder:solvent 1:5), filtered and solvent removed at 40°C; phenolic fraction extracted from oil with methanol/water (60:40)
sample_size: One Maazoun cultivar oil sample; analytical determinations in triplicate (n=3; not independent biological samples)
source_title: Cucumis melo L. seeds as a promising source of oil naturally rich in biologically active substances: compositional characteristics, phenolic compounds and thermal properties
database_reference: Table 4: Amentoflavone 3.88 ± 0.11 mg/100 g; triplicate determinations. Methods 2.11: compounds matched to standards, commercial standards used, amounts as mg/100 g DW.
extraction_notes: The measured matrix is seed oil, not intact seed or melon pulp. Authors describe melon seed oil as edible and report sensory testing; they state it can be used in culinary preparations and food formulations. The sample is experimental Maazoun cultivar oil, not a retail market survey.
uncertainty_notes: Reported mean ± SD is 3.88 ± 0.11 mg/100 g (normalized mean 38.8 mg/kg; SD 1.1 mg/kg). Triplicates are analytical determinations; biological/sample-to-sample variability is not established. Methods describe results on dry weight basis; do not infer general melon-seed-oil population mean.
